learning_objectives: Explain the concept of Corrective RAG, understand its working mechanism, and identify its benefits in reducing AI hallucinations.
outline: Understanding the feedback loop in Corrective RAG.
How Corrective RAG verifies and revises answers.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and what AI hallucinations are.

slides.title: Title Slide
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Corrective **RAG** – Self-Correcting **AI**.
slides.image_prompt: Title slide with 'Corrective RAG – Self-Correcting AI' prominently displayed, perhaps with gears and a magnifying glass icon.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to explain the concept of Corrective **RAG**.
You will understand its working mechanism.
And identify its benefits in reducing **AI hallucinations**.
slides.image_prompt: Learning objectives listed clearly on the slide.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you should have a basic understanding of **Retrieval-Augmented Generation**, or **RAG**.
You should also know what **AI hallucinations** are.
slides.image_prompt: Prerequisites listed on the slide, perhaps with book or knowledge icons.

slides.title: Introduction to Corrective RAG
slides.narration:
Have you ever seen an **AI** give a confidently wrong answer?
This is called an **AI hallucination**.
Corrective **RAG** is an advanced technique.
It helps **AI** models avoid these mistakes.
It makes **AI** self-correcting.
slides.image_prompt: A confused robot thinking, then a corrected, confident robot smiling, illustrating the concept of self-correction.

slides.title: Key Idea: The Feedback Loop
slides.narration:
The core idea behind Corrective **RAG** is a feedback loop.
Think of it as the **AI** checking its own homework.
It does not just give an answer.
It first checks if the answer is accurate.
It uses the information it already retrieved.
slides.image_prompt: A diagram showing a circular arrow representing a feedback loop, with an **AI** model icon inside, emphasizing the verification process.

slides.title: How It Works: Step 1 - Initial Answer
slides.narration:
Let's see how Corrective **RAG** works.
First, the **AI** model generates an initial answer.
This is like a first draft.
It uses its knowledge and the retrieved documents.
slides.image_prompt: An **AI** icon generating text, with a thought bubble showing a preliminary, unverified answer.

slides.title: How It Works: Step 2 - Cross-Checking
slides.narration:
Next, the **AI** cross-checks this initial answer.
It compares it with the retrieved documents.
It asks: "Is this answer supported by the facts I found?"
This is its internal "fact-checking" step.
slides.image_prompt: An **AI** icon with two documents, one representing the initial answer and the other retrieved evidence, with arrows comparing them for consistency.

slides.title: How It Works: Step 3 - Revision
slides.narration:
If the **AI** finds any inconsistencies, it revises the response.
It corrects any unsupported statements.
This ensures the final answer is accurate.
It is like editing its own work before submitting it.
slides.image_prompt: An **AI** icon with a pencil and eraser, revising a document, showing a corrected and accurate answer being produced.

slides.title: Benefits: Reduced Hallucinations
slides.narration:
What are the benefits of Corrective **RAG**?
It significantly reduces **AI hallucinations**.
This means fewer made-up facts.
The **AI** becomes much more reliable.
slides.image_prompt: A graph showing a downward trend in 'hallucinations' with an **AI** icon looking satisfied, emphasizing error reduction.

slides.title: Benefits: Increased Reliability
slides.narration:
This approach also increases factual reliability.
You can trust the **AI's** outputs more.
It builds confidence in the information provided.
This is crucial for critical applications.
slides.image_prompt: A shield icon with a checkmark, next to an **AI** icon, symbolizing trust, accuracy, and increased confidence in **AI** outputs.

slides.title: Analogy: Built-in Fact-Checker
content: Like an AI with a built-in “fact-checking” layer.
Ensures every statement is supported by source material.
slides.narration:
Think of Corrective **RAG** like this:
It's an **AI** with a built-in fact-checker.
Every statement is double-checked.
It must be supported by the source material.
This ensures accuracy before it speaks.
slides.image_prompt: A magnifying glass inspecting a document, with an **AI** icon in the background, illustrating the 'fact-checking' layer.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned about Corrective **RAG**.
We saw how its feedback loop works.
And we explored its benefits in making **AI** more reliable.
slides.image_prompt: Summary slide with bullet points recapping the main learning points.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Research a recent example of **AI hallucination**.
Think about how Corrective **RAG** could have prevented it.
Write down your findings.
